Definition: from G1223 and G5055; to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to persist:--continue.
BiblicalUsage: To continue is to keep at a thing until it is done, and the word stands once, where Paul and his companions continue fasting until the fourteenth day of the storm. They had eaten nothing for two weeks, and Paul urges them to eat for their health.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that continuing through the storm is the whole voyage in one word; the wind did not stop, the ship did not mend, but the men kept on, and the God who kept them through fourteen days brought them safe to land.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
